title: Apex fallback clarity and replay instructions (customer-facing)
content:
Executive summary:

On 2026-09-15 between 09:03 and 09:57 UTC we observed degraded responses for a subset of tenant inference requests in our eu-west and us-central regions. Symptoms included partial token truncation for structured outputs and intermittent longer tail latencies for streaming calls. Approximately 1.8% of requests in the impacted window returned incomplete top-level objects or early stream termination. No customer data exfiltration or mutating storage corruption was detected.

Severity: Moderate (service-affecting for a small fraction of requests; customer-visible integrity issues for structured/streaming responses).

Immediate customer-facing status page update (proposed short message):

Title: Partial structured-response truncation affecting a subset of requests — mitigation in progress
Status: Degraded performance — service routing and fallbacks enabled
Start: 2026-09-15 09:03 UTC
Current update (09:40 UTC): We have enabled fallback routing to alternate model variants and a routing-only mode for impacted regions. This reduces error surface but may change latency/quality tradeoffs for affected tenants. Teams are continuing validation; customers may observe shortened streams or alternate model outputs while routing is active. We will post a final closure note after validation.

Why this matters (one-sentence): A small percentage of inference calls returned incomplete structured payloads during failover routing, which may affect downstream parsers expecting fully-formed objects.

Customer-facing postmortem (concise):

What happened: During a regional capacity rebalancing triggered by transient host flaps, the serving runtime selected a model variant with an incompatible KV-cache serialization feature flag for some active sessions. When the system performed automated fallback to maintain throughput (apex fallback routing), a subset of live sessions resumed on nodes that did not correctly hydrate prefix/KV cache entries for multi-turn structured outputs. The result: some streaming sessions terminated early or produced truncated JSON-like top-level objects.

Impact: 1.8% of inference requests in the 54-minute window returned truncated or incomplete structured outputs. Approximately 400 unique tenants saw at least one affected call. The majority of affected calls were for streaming chat and structured generation (function-calling / JSON output). No PII or customer data was exposed beyond normal request/response flows.

Root cause (short): An unsafe KV-cache serialization regression combined with an automated routing policy that allowed live session migration without cache compatibility checks.

Root cause (details):
- A recent runtime change (kernel selection and cache serialization param GH-rruntime-291) introduced a new binary serialization format for in-memory KV caches that improves performance for long contexts.
- The change rolled into a canary pool and then mixed-capacity hosts during a staggered autoscale event.
- The apex fallback routing logic attempts to preserve session continuity by moving active sessions to available capacity; it did not validate the receiving host's cache compatibility for the new serialization variant.
- When sessions were migrated, the receiver nodes treated legacy cache blobs as invalid and dropped prefix entries. This led to early stream termination and truncated outputs when the model expected cached context to generate complete structured payloads.

Mitigation (immediate):
- At 09:12 UTC we disabled apex fallback session migration for live streaming routes and enforced strict host cache-compatibility checks before migration.
- At 09:27 UTC we pushed an emergency validation to the routing layer that rejects migration if cache-serialization-format mismatch is detected.
- We started a targeted replay of affected requests (see Customer options below) and enabled an alternate model variant (compatible-serialization) as a temporary routing target.

Verification: Operator checks and automated tests indicate that after changes, no further truncation events were observed for two consecutive 15-minute windows (09:30–10:00 UTC and 10:00–10:15 UTC). We are continuing a longer-running synthetic workload test across regions before declaring full remediation.

Customer options and recommended actions (how customers can verify and request remediation):
1) Quick verification steps (self-serve):
   - If you notice truncated JSON-like objects or early stream termination in logs, filter requests by timestamp (2026-09-15 09:03–09:57 UTC) and model route identifier.
   - For structured outputs, confirm top-level keys are present and that streaming sessions reached final 'stop' events. If missing keys are observed, mark the request as candidate for replay.

2) Replay option (recommended for affected tenants):
   - We are offering an opt-in replay where we re-run your affected requests on a compatible model variant with preserved context where available. Replays are limited to the original request payloads and will not attempt to reprocess external side effects.
   - To request replays: open a support ticket with subject line "Replay request — incident 2026-09-15 apex fallback" and include (a) up to 500 example request IDs or a time-range + route; (b) tenant org id; (c) preferred retention policy for evidence. Our CS team will queue replays and provide an evidence bundle including before/after response diffs.

3) Self-retry guidance (if you prefer to run replays yourself):
   - Re-run the original request against the same model ID but include the query param &redwood-mode=compatible-serialization or set the SDK flag session_cache_compat=true. This will route requests to nodes with legacy-friendly cache handling.
   - Note: replays may result in different surface-level tokenization/latency; compare by functional tests (schema validators) rather than token-level diffs.

Evidence & verification package (what we provide):
- For tenants that request replay, we will provide: replay schedule, before/after response samples, operator timeline, and the routing decision log for affected requests.
- For enterprise accounts with audit needs we can provide signed evidence packages and an operator-signed timeline.

Planned long-term fixes (roadmap):
- 1) Revert or standardize to a single stable KV-cache serialization format across the fleet and add an explicit compatibility flag to model variants (Q4 2026).
- 2) Add schema-level session migration validation in the routing plane so a migration attempt assesses prefix hydratability before moving live sessions (priority: P0).
- 3) Expand synthetic end-to-end tests to include structured-output integrity during failover scenarios and model-variant switches.
- 4) Post-deployment: a staged rollout policy that gates apex fallback routing changes behind cross-region synthetic checks.

Customer-facing timeline (high level):
- 09:03 UTC — initial alerts: increased error counts for structured output validators in eu-west and us-central.
- 09:09 UTC — on-call acknowledges, begins scope and triage.
- 09:12 UTC — apex fallback session migration paused; emergency routing guard enabled.
- 09:27 UTC — compatibility reject rule deployed to routing layer.
- 09:35 UTC — compatible-serialization variant enabled as alternate route for impacted traffic.
- 09:57 UTC — operator-level blameless review begins; synthetic validation started.
- 10:15 UTC — two successive 15-minute verification windows passed; monitoring remains in watch mode.

Questions customers commonly ask (FAQ snippets we can paste into customer replies):
Q: Will replay change the semantics of my data or cause duplicates?
A: Replays re-run inference only — they do not invoke customer-side side effects. If your application relies on idempotent downstream actions, treat replayed outputs as new predictions and reconcile per your application logic.

Q: How long will the alternate routing remain in effect?
A: We will keep the compatible-serialization variant available until the fleetwide standardization/validation rollout completes. We expect this to be resolved in the Q4 standardization window; we will provide periodic updates.

Q: Will we receive credits or SLA adjustments?
A: If you believe SLA impact meets your contract thresholds, open a ticket with billing & CS and we will begin a credit assessment per your agreement.

Next steps for us (operator commitments):
- Complete fleet standardization proposal by 2026-09-22 and share with customers who opt in for technical review.
- Provide a replay evidence bundle within 72 hours for customers who request it.
- Publish a formal customer postmortem (long-form) with code references and remediation timelines by 2026-09-23.

Notes to internal ops (not for customer-facing copy):
- Follow up with GH-rruntime-291 revert/patch patchset and prepare canary with compatibility checks before re-enabling apex migration.
- Cross-team: SRE + serving-runtime + routing + product to align on gating rules and telemetry for session migration.

Draft sign-off (who needs to review for publish):
- Customer Success (Maya Singh), Serving Runtime (Liam Chen), SRE (Sofia Martinez), Legal (for evidence package language), Product (hosted api lead).

Tracking keys / references: incident id INC-2026-09-APEX, runtime PR GH-rruntime-291, confluence page CONFLUENCE-4821.

End of document.
